agree.reason: The page reads as credible and salon-specific, but this owner pays her cousin $600 a year, and nothing here explains why she should pay $2,388 a year or tells her she can keep her cousin, so she would probably not book the call.

honest.reason: No numbers are invented, but the page promises books 'on time' without saying the 10th was missed three times last year, and 'the rest of the week is for my clients' is filler the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: The raw facts are repeated without working them out: there's no annual cost, no retention rate (2 of 33, both sales), no share of clients who saved at tax time (9 of 31), and no comparison of the $800 saving against the fee.

right_comparison.reason: The page never describes the reader's actual alternative, which is a once-a-year tax-time catch-up by a relative, and it never contrasts that with monthly books, payroll and sales tax filing.

qualification.reason: The guarantee is checkable, with a date (the 10th) and a consequence (that month is free), and the accountant-savings claim is hedged properly, but the no-contract, 30-day-notice exit is left out.

objections.reason: Her main objections are cost and loyalty to her cousin, and the page meets neither: it never says Carla doesn't do income tax returns, so the cousin keeps that work and gets clean books from her, and it doesn't mention the easy exit.

fit.reason: It is about 350 words of sales-page body text with clear sections and the booking button at the end, as the brief asked.
